title: Bit-slice Architecture for DNN Acceleration with Slice-level Sparsity Enhancement and Exploitation
problem: Existing bit-slice DNN accelerator architectures exploit sparsity only at coarse granularity — either input or weight sparsity independently — failing to simultaneously leverage both input and weight sparsity at fine (bit-slice chunk) granularity, leaving substantial computational savings unrealized.
motivation: Bit-slice architectures offer high reconfigurability for mixed-precision DNN inference, but their fine-grained sparsity potential is underutilized due to hardware complexity in jointly handling both input and weight slice-level zeros.
method: The BADA architecture splits numbers into bit-slices (the individual bit layers within each number) and uses a front-end unit (the first processing stage) to select only non-zero slices before computation. It skips calculations in two ways: when an entire chunk of bits is zero, and when either the input or weight has a zero bit-slice at any position (catching both types of empty space at once). The system represents each bit-slice using 8 bits without needing extra hardware—better than the 6-7 bit limit in earlier designs—and during training it adjusts weight distributions to create more zeros in higher-order bit-slices, amplifying the sparsity gains.
key_novelty: The core innovation is using a front-end selection mechanism to exploit both input and weight sparsity simultaneously at the bit-slice level, paired with training that concentrates zeros into higher-order bit-slices.
contributions: BADA architecture jointly leveraging coarse- and fine-grained input and weight sparsity at the bit-slice level.
Front-end non-zero slice selection unit enabling skip of any operand pair with a zero input or weight slice.
8-bit data representation for bit-slice architectures without additional hardware overhead (vs. 6-7 bit in prior art).
Training-time weight distribution narrowing to increase zero-valued higher-order bit-slice proportion; 2.67x throughput, 1.52x area efficiency, 2.15x energy efficiency vs. LUTein.
limitations: The weight distribution narrowing training technique adds training-time cost and may reduce model accuracy for tasks where weight magnitude diversity is important; evaluation scope (specific DNN models) is not detailed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Joint input-weight bit-slice sparsity exploitation for DNN acceleration
